summary.short: Exempts electricity, equipment and software used in large single-occupant Texas data centers from state sales and use tax for 10 or 15 years, if the Comptroller certifies the center and it creates 20 well-paid jobs and invests at least $200 million.
summary.long: Section 151.359 of the Texas Tax Code exempts from state sales and use tax the tangible personal property necessary to operate a qualifying data center: electricity, electrical and cooling systems, generators, servers, storage, network equipment, racks, software and related components. A data center must occupy at least 100,000 square feet in a single building used by a single qualifying occupant. Certification by the Comptroller requires that, on or after 1 September 2013, the occupant, owner or operator create at least 20 qualifying jobs in the county, paying at least 120% of the county average weekly wage, and invest at least $200 million over five years. The exemption runs from certification for 10 years, or 15 years if investment reaches $250 million. Office supplies, short leases, taxable services and local sales taxes are excluded, as are centers with former Chapter 313 value-limitation agreements. Registration numbers are revoked if requirements are not met, and the taxes become due with penalty and interest.
